launcher: Fixed later generations, Gen 6 types and Battle Revolution models not reaching the game in Colosseum and XD when you had many of them on at once, such as Replace all models with Generation 4 and 6 Pokémon. If the game's Pokémon still come to more than the game can read, the launcher leaves out Replace all models and says so in the log, or tells you what to turn off, instead of starting the game without them.

Fixed the Pokédex showing stale types, abilities, or base stats after changing Battle rules, Generation 4/5/6 Pokémon, or Customize rules settings: it now refreshes automatically and shows updated Gen 4 and Gen 6 abilities, hidden abilities, Fairy types, and Gen 6 base stats right away.

Edit Pokémon on the Pokémon tab now supports Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon (Victini to Volcanion and their alternate forms), their moves and held items, Fairy-type moves and hidden abilities whenever those settings are turned on under Gameplay.
Customize rules under Settings → Gameplay now opens expanded by default instead of collapsed.

Fixed "Launcher update check failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'battleRules')" in the top bar, which showed when your save had a Story party and your online room was set to Diamond and Pearl battle rules. The Story party's Pokémon that a room for both games can't take are listed under X and Y rules too.

Later generations are simpler to set up under Gameplay: each generation's switch has its disc or ROM right below it, and their models, icons and cries are made by themselves when you choose it, turn the generation on or update the game, so the Make assets buttons are gone. HD textures under Graphics is now the one switch for every HD texture: with it on, your Battle Revolution and 3DS models get their own textures too, downloaded once their models are made, in place of a switch for each.

Gen 6 types: the Fairy type and generation 6's type chart, in Colosseum and XD, under any battle rules. Clefairy, Gardevoir, Togepi, Marill, Mawile and the other Pokémon that became Fairy types are Fairy types, and so are Charm, Sweet Kiss and Moonlight; Dragon moves don't affect them, and Steel types no longer resist Ghost and Dark moves. Fairy Wind, Disarming Voice, Draining Kiss, Play Rough, Moonblast, Dazzling Gleam and Baby-Doll Eyes are new moves, learned at the levels they are in generation 6; Pokémon already in your save are Fairy types too, and can remember a Fairy move they're past the level for from the Move Deleter on Mt. Battle (XD's Move Teacher). Turn it on under Gameplay, in Customize rules below Battle rules; X and Y battle rules have it already. The Pokédex and team builder show it, and an online room has it when its host turns it on under Customize rules.

X and Y battle rules: under Gameplay, Battle rules can now be X and Y (Gen 6), with every move, ability and held item of generations 5 and 6, generation 6's damage, critical hits, sleep, Protect, multi-hit moves, weather abilities lasting 5 turns, Electric types that can't be paralyzed, Grass types unaffected by powder moves, Ghost types that escape traps, sound moves through substitutes, Knock Off, Defog, Sturdy, Lightning Rod, Oblivious, Stench, Mental Herb and other move, ability and item changes, its higher base stats for Pikachu, Clefable, Alakazam and others, its level-up moves, and hidden abilities such as Ninetales' Drought. To mix generations, open Customize rules below Battle rules and turn any of them on or off.

Online rooms can play by X and Y battle rules, and the host can turn any of them on or off under Customize rules, below Rules. Battle rules have the same three names in Settings and on the Online page: Colosseum (Gen 3), Diamond and Pearl (Gen 4) and X and Y (Gen 6). The team builder has Generation 6 parties, which can have the Pokémon of generations 4, 5 and 6 and all their moves, learn moves as in X and Y, can have a hidden ability, and can hold the items generations 5 and 6 brought, such as Assault Vest, Air Balloon, Eject Button and Safety Goggles.

Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon: a new switch under Gameplay, below Generation 4 Pokémon, adds the 228 Pokémon from Victini to Volcanion, with their stats, abilities, hidden abilities and moves, to the Pokédex and the game. Their own moves and abilities play under X and Y battle rules, and their 3D models (lit and shaded like the game's own, with glowing flames in their own colours, such as Mega Charizard X's blue fire, and Primal Kyogre's glowing lines), shiny variants, battle faces and Pokédex pictures drawn from those models as the game's own are, icons and cries can be made, along with every other form the 3DS games have (Megas, Primal Reversion, Alola forms, female looks, battle forms and every Vivillon pattern), which the Pokédex's Look menu shows with each form's own types, stats and abilities (a new Shiny switch beside it shows any look shiny), and the team builder shows a shiny Pokémon's own sprite straight from your own decrypted Pokémon Ultra Sun, Ultra Moon, Sun or Moon 3DS ROM under Gameplay, without Blender. Feebas, Spritzee and Swirlix evolve when traded holding a Prism Scale, Sachet or Whipped Dream, and trades carry Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon, moves and items when both games have them turned on.

Generations 5 and 6 across the launcher: the randomizer can now pick Gen 5 and Gen 6 Pokémon, Colosseum and XD crossplay online rooms support Gen 5 and 6 Pokémon, moves, items, Fairy moves and hidden abilities under X and Y rules, Shadowtrade carries Gen 5 and 6 Shadow Pokémon for players who have them turned on, and the team builder lists up to 700 Pokémon at once.

3DS HD textures: your 3DS models of Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon and of every other form the 3DS games have (Mega Evolutions, Alola forms, female models and the rest) can show the 3DS games' own textures, upscaled for sharper detail, in both games and the Pokédex. It's a one-time download of about 845 MB that comes with HD textures, once their models are made.

Battle lighting: in battle, Pokémon and trainers are lit from the front and a little brighter, so their faces and fronts aren't left in shadow. It's on for Colosseum and XD; turn it off under Graphics.
X and Y rules: Poison Gas and Cotton Spore hit both opposing Pokémon in a double battle, as they do from generation 5.

Later base stats now also give every Pokémon its base experience from generation 5 on, so Blissey, Garchomp and the other Pokémon that were stingy with experience in Platinum give what they do in X and Y.
Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon can use the game's own TMs for any move they learn in X and Y by TM, tutor or level, such as Iron Tail and Water Pulse.
Smeargle can Sketch generation 5 and 6 moves in the team builder and in online legality checks.
Fletchinder's name in the game is FLETCHINDR, not a cut-off FLETCHINDE.
Online legality under X and Y rules allows 252 EVs in a stat, generation 6's most; a story Pokémon with up to 255 goes as 252, which makes the same stat.

Import from Black, White, Black 2 and White 2 saves, and from decrypted X, Y, Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire saves: their party and PC boxes come over under Pokémon → Import, keeping each Pokémon's nature, gender, shininess and hidden ability where the game can.

Eevee can evolve into Leafeon with a Leaf Stone, into Glaceon by levelling up holding NeverMeltIce, and into Sylveon by levelling up with high friendship knowing a Fairy move; Pancham evolves at level 32 with a Dark type in the party.

The Pokédex says how a Pokémon evolves in this game and, where that's a stand-in, how it evolves in X and Y, Black and White or Platinum (Malamar upside down, Goodra in the rain, Tyrantrum by day, the Dusk and Shiny Stones).

Forms with their own stats are Pokémon of their own with Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon: Deoxys's Attack, Defense and Speed Formes, Rotom's five appliances, Giratina's Origin Forme, Shaymin's Sky Forme, the Therian Formes, Black and White Kyurem, Hoopa Unbound, Wormadam's cloaks, Basculin's blue stripes, Pumpkaboo's and Gourgeist's sizes and female Meowstic, each with its own stats, types, abilities, moves and 3DS model, in the team builder, online and in your saves.

Change form: on the Pokémon page, a Deoxys, Rotom, Giratina, Shaymin, Tornadus, Thundurus, Landorus, Kyurem or Hoopa in your save can change form with the game closed, standing in for the Meteorite, Rotom Catalog, Gracidea, Reveal Glass, DNA Splicers and Prison Bottle until the story has them. Kyurem, Rotom and Hoopa swap their own moves as they do in the 3DS games.
A female Espurr evolves into a female Meowstic, and Pumpkaboo of each size into Gourgeist of the same size.
Importing from a DS or 3DS save brings a Pokémon's form along (Wash Rotom, Therian Landorus, Black Kyurem, a female Meowstic) with Generation 5 and 6 Pokémon.
Generation 6 moves whose names were cut off mid-word in battle have names that fit, such as PHANTOMFORCE, LIGHTOFRUIN and THOUS.ARROWS.
Choosing the Story party online with a Generation 5 or 6 Pokémon in it switches the room to X and Y battle rules, as one with a Generation 4 Pokémon switches to Diamond and Pearl rules.

e-Reader cards on the Pokémon page (Colosseum): import your e-Reader card dumps or use a folder of them, see which levels of each card your save has won, and pick the card your next scan in the game gives, to replay a fight you lost or play one you skipped.
game: Fixed later generations, Gen 6 types and Battle Revolution models not loading when you had many of them on at once. If the launcher's Pokémon can't be read, the game now stops with a message instead of starting without them, which made saved Pokémon forget their later generations' moves.

Gen 6 types: with the setting on, both games have the Fairy type, with generation 6's type chart, a Fairy type picture in each game's own style on every screen that shows types, and its new moves, Draining Kiss giving back three quarters of the damage. With it off again, a Pokémon that learned a Fairy move forgets it, leaving the slot empty, and the same for a Generation 4 move with Generation 4 off, so a save from either still loads.

Generation 6 mechanics in Colosseum and XD: each of X and Y's battle changes plays when the launcher turns it on, with damage worked out as Pokémon Showdown does, Assault Vest, Eviolite, Rocky Helmet and Weakness Policy as held items, and a Pokémon's hidden ability in online battles.

Generation 5 and 6 battles in Colosseum and XD: under X and Y rules, every move, ability and held item of generations 5 and 6 plays as it does in X and Y. That covers moves from Scald, Volt Switch and Shell Smash to the terrains, Sticky Web, King's Shield, Wide Guard, Pledge combinations, Sky Drop lifting its target, and After You, Quash and Ally Switch in double battles; abilities such as Prankster, Magic Bounce, Regenerator, Moxie, Protean and Symbiosis, with Aegislash, Darmanitan and Meloetta changing form in battle; and items such as Air Balloon, Eject Button and Red Card. Older moves and abilities change as they did in those games too: Feint hits without Protect, Tailwind lasts 4 turns, Growth raises Sp. Atk as well, a missed Hi Jump Kick costs half the user's HP, Cotton Guard and Tail Glow raise a stat drastically in one step, Wish heals half of the user's max HP, Future Sight and Doom Desire calculate damage with types when they land, Beat Up hits as a Dark-type physical move, and Pickup recovers consumed items in battle.

Generations 5 and 6 in the randomizer, XD Poké Spots and crossplay: both games' randomizer and XD's expanded Poké Spots now include Gen 5 and Gen 6 Pokémon (with their legendaries respected and Eevee able to evolve into Sylveon), and crossplay online rooms between Colosseum and XD carry Gen 5 and 6 Pokémon, moves and items under X and Y rules.

Fixed XD crashing on startup or missing pack cries and custom hero models when hundreds of Pokémon models (such as Gen 4 and Gen 5-6 together) were loaded: the virtual disc overlay space is now ten times larger.
Pokémon and trainers in battle can be lit from the front and a little brighter instead of mostly from above and behind (the launcher's Battle lighting setting).

X and Y battles play closer to the real games: Magic Bounce reflects the new status moves, Substitute blocks the ones it should and Hyperspace Hole gets past it, Metronome can call any move of generations 1 to 6, Heal Block stops draining moves, and Scald and Steam Eruption thaw their user.

X and Y battles: U-turn and Volt Switch set off the target's Rocky Helmet, Air Balloon, Red Card, Eject Button and other items; an Air Balloon floats over Spikes, Sticky Web and the terrains; Thousand Arrows hits a floating Pokémon; Rocky Helmet hurts on every hit of a multi-hit move.

X and Y battles: Unnerve stops every Berry, Harvest and Cheek Pouch work with every kind of Berry, Belch counts a Berry eaten before a switch, Sheer Force takes away Fake Out's flinch, Defiant and Competitive answer Intimidate, Sticky Web and King's Shield, and Trace, Role Play, Skill Swap and Gastro Acid leave Stance Change, Illusion and the other protected abilities alone.

X and Y battles: Natural Gift, Flail, Reversal, Oblivion Wing, Chatter, Autotomize, Low Kick and Grass Knot, Psyshock, Plus and Minus, Mud Sport and Water Sport, Defog against Sticky Web, Arceus with a Pixie Plate, Misty Terrain, Magic Guard, Heal Pulse, Wide Guard, Fling, Incinerate, Clear Smog, Rage Powder, Round, Struggle and move accuracy now work as they do in X and Y.
Level-up moves past a Pokémon's twentieth are learned too (Deoxys's Psycho Boost, Steelix's Stone Edge), and the Move Deleter and XD's Move Teacher can remind them.
Giratina holding a Griseous Orb battles in its Origin Forme, with Levitate, under X and Y rules; Hoopa can use Hyperspace Fury only as Hoopa Unbound.
Aegislash, Darmanitan and Meloetta change their 3DS model when they change form in battle (Blade Forme, Zen Mode, Pirouette Forme).

X and Y battles: Poison Touch no longer gets past Shield Dust, Leaf Guard, Flower Veil or Misty Terrain, Cursed Body works as its holder faints, Gooey respects Clear Body and Mist, Mold Breaker gets past Contrary and Simple, Aroma Veil stops Cursed Body and Cute Charm, and Download counts a foe behind a substitute.

Trainers judge each Generation 4, 5 and 6 move by what it does, in both games: Light of Ruin as a strong attack instead of a healing move, Drill Run as an attack instead of a one-hit KO, Quiver Dance as a stat boost, Heal Pulse as a move they rarely use, while each move keeps its own animation.

X and Y battles: the end of each turn goes effect by effect as it does in X and Y, in both games and online between them: Wish and Future Sight land first, then every Pokémon's Shed Skin, Hydration or Healer and its Leftovers or Black Sludge, then Leech Seed, then poison and burns, with Reflect, Light Screen and the like wearing off after those.

X and Y battles: Infiltrator gets past Safeguard and Mist, Crafty Shield also stops a partner's status moves and ones Protect lets through, such as Transform, Mean Look and Block, Imposter copies the foe across from it in double battles, Payback isn't doubled against a Pokémon that just came in, Liquid Ooze hurts a Pokémon using Dream Eater, Rototiller doesn't fail while a Pokémon is in the air, Mold Breaker gets past Telepathy and the auras, Electro Ball goes by each Pokémon's Speed at the time, and Eviolite and Assault Vest work with Platinum's damage too.
Fixed the starter picker in XD leaving blank portraits on pages when later generations are enabled.

Colosseum-e card battles from the Japanese release: Phenac Stadium's left door now opens to the e-Reader reception, where dumps of your own e-Reader cards scan without a Game Boy Advance, with every level, Poké Coupon and item reward, and the VR TRAINERS' Shadow Togepi, Mareep and Scizor to snag. Each scan gives the card with the easiest level left to win, so a fight you lost or skipped comes back after the others.
Fixed e-Reader card battles writing over their own saved data, which showed a difficulty tab's name as a white box.

releases.title: Online co-op and Poké Spot fixes

changes: Fixed online co-op battles going out of step and leaving the joining player stuck in the fight. The host's battle and Gameplay settings now decide, and a Pokémon either player snags or catches ends up in both games.
Fixed Pokémon XD crashing when you continue a save made at a Poké Spot during a visit. It happened when the visitor came from More Poké Spot Pokémon.

launcher: Pokémon: a new tab shows your party and every PC box with each Pokémon's sprite, level, HP, friendship and heart gauge. While the game runs it shows them live.

Shadowtrade: send a Shadow Pokémon and receive one another player sent, still to be purified. Colosseum and XD players trade across games, including Generation 4 Shadows, and each arrives in its own slot so story Shadows stay snaggable.
Online Trades: trade any purified Pokémon with a friend by code across Colosseum and XD. Trade evolutions play with your game's own scene, whether your game is running or closed.
Trades between your games: move Pokémon directly between your Colosseum and XD saves side by side from the Pokémon tab, with trade evolutions included.

Import from a GBA or DS save: open a Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed, LeafGreen, Diamond, Pearl or Platinum save on the Pokémon tab and copy Pokémon into Colosseum or XD. The original save is left untouched.

Edit save Pokémon: edit any Pokémon's species, level, moves, item, ability, nature, EVs, IVs, nickname or shiny status on the Pokémon tab while the game is closed. Edited Pokémon are marked, blocked from Shadowtrade and flagged in Online Trades.

Online co-op: play the story together over the network from the Online page's new Co-op Story tab, or host your active save from in-game START → Settings → Co-op. Share a code or list it in the public lobby, with no port forwarding needed.
Split-screen co-op: choose player 2's hero, side-by-side or stacked split, and whether the keyboard stays player 1 under Gameplay. Co-op is on by default in Colosseum and XD.

Difficulty: raise story trainers' levels, evolve their teams, enlarge teams and add Shadows. Scale levels by up to 50% or above your strongest Pokémon and add up to 48 more Shadow Pokémon under Gameplay, included in randomizer spoilers.
Replace all models: give Bulbasaur to Deoxys their Pokémon Battle Revolution models too. Works in both games and the Pokédex; turn it on under Gameplay, beside Battle Revolution assets.

Battle Revolution HD textures: download upscaled textures from Pokémon Battle Revolution (about 275 MB) for sharper models in both games and the Pokédex. Turn it on under Gameplay, below Battle Revolution assets.

Jukebox visualizer: dancing Ludicolo react to each song's beat, drops and tone. They perform in the Purification Chamber (XD) or the gold star hall (Colosseum) alongside Miror B.; toggle Visualizer or Hide overlay in the header.
Jukebox: songs start sooner, build faster and fade smoothly into one another. Press Pop out to open the Jukebox and visualizer in its own window without stopping the music.
Make a pack: copy any Pokémon in the Pokédex straight into your packs folder. It brings along its stats, moves, evolutions, model and sprites ready to edit.
Pokémon packs: pack Pokémon can now evolve from any of the game's own Pokémon and use every evolution method the game has, including Tyrogue's, Wurmple's, Shedinja's and Feebas's.
Customize: May and Leaf now have Lips and Eyeshadow colours. Red's and Leaf's colour labels also name every part they change.
Add to Steam: Pokémon XD now gets its full Steam artwork, including library cover, header, logo and icon. Select "In your Steam library" on the main screen to update an existing XD shortcut.
Portable launcher: Settings now explains why it can't self-update or join Beta. Use Get the installer to open the releases page.
Controls: moving an analog stick while binding a button now explains that sticks can't be bound.
Fixed Customize leaving stray colour patches on heroes and faces reverting when blinking. Reflections on Wes's and Michael's gear also keep their colours with HD textures.
Fixed custom heroes in XD standing still while pushing crates and jumping down from them. They now move as Michael does on the S.S. Libra.
Fixed Pokémon XD song names in the Jukebox and songs looping a fraction of a second early. The Title Screen and Demo Opening tracks are no longer swapped.
Fixed Settings → Controls on Windows reporting an unstarted Wii U GameCube adapter as ready. It now guides WinUSB setup with Zadig, and the game log notes what Windows sees.
Fixed game builds failing or freezing on PCs with many CPU cores and limited memory. Builds now cap parallel jobs to available memory.
Fixed A and B being swapped when navigating with a Switch Pro Controller or Joy-Con.
Fixed the Story party on the Online page leaving out Generation 4 Pokémon. XD's Bonsly and Munchlax also come along under Platinum's rules.
Fixed Pokédex 3D models with scaled limb rigs showing oversized, distorted hands and legs. Affects models such as Sableye and Ralts.

changes: 120 fps: choose 30, 60 or 120 fps under Settings → Display or in-game Settings in Colosseum and XD. Characters, the camera, fades and Snag Balls run twice as smoothly at normal speed, and in-game changes save to the launcher.

Split-screen co-op: press START on a second controller in the field to join in Colosseum or XD with your own camera and half of the screen. Explore together, choose for the second Pokémon in double battles, hold START to leave, Z to regroup or X to swap hero.
Online co-op: two players share one story across the network in Colosseum and XD, moving through doors, cutscenes and double battles side by side. The joining player saves to a separate memory card.

Trade arrivals: incoming trades show a P★DA-style notice, evolution and summary card in the field. Shiny Shadow Pokémon from Shadowtrade look shiny right away, and purifying a story Shadow copy counts toward Ho-Oh in Colosseum.

Exp All: battlers earn normal EXP and the rest of your party gets an adjustable share. Shown in one party panel with level-ups in Colosseum and XD; held EXP. SHARE adds on top, and you can turn it on under Gameplay.
Infinite TMs: teaching a TM no longer uses it up, in Colosseum and XD. Turn it on under Gameplay.
Move Relearner: the Move Deleter in Colosseum lets Pokémon remember level-up moves without Gen 4 on. Find him at Mt. Battle's Pokémon Center; on by default under Gameplay.
GBA trades from the start: Phenac City's and Gateon Port's Trade Centers now trade with your GBA save before finishing the story. On by default under Settings → Game Boy Advance.
Shiny odds: choose shiny odds from 1 in 8192 up to 1 in 32 under Gameplay. Counts for starters, Shadow Pokémon and XD's Poké Spot Pokémon in both games.
More Poké Spot Pokémon: in XD, each Poké Spot can now attract about 60 species sorted by type, including Generation 4 Pokémon when enabled. On by default under Gameplay.
C-Stick moves like the Control Stick: in Colosseum, walk and navigate menus with the C-Stick as in XD for one-handed play. Turn it on under Controls.

Battle Revolution models: major overhaul to shading, reflections, eyes, shinies and effects. Models gain fire, gas and sparkles from your disc and proper back-face culling; Make assets offers to remake them and skips failures.
In-game Settings' Fullscreen resolution list no longer offers sizes smaller than 640×480.
Fixed Colosseum and XD crashing when an opponent's Pokémon knows Heal Bell or Aromatherapy. That includes the final battle with Miror B. in XD.
Fixed Colosseum and XD crashing in battles with large Battle Revolution or pack models. Both games reserve more model memory and reload skipped models once room frees up.
Fixed battles freezing when a Battle Revolution model used a move with its own animation. Moves like Pichu's Tail Whip now play out normally.
Fixed XD crashing in some double battles while the opponent chose its moves. That includes battle 91 on Mt. Battle.
Fixed XD crashing when opening the Strategy Memo with more than 400 Pokémon.
Fixed being unable to jump down from ledges and crates in XD at 60 fps. The hero now steps off ledges on the S.S. Libra instead of walking in place.
Fixed people in Colosseum cutscenes sometimes walking on the spot at 60 and 120 fps. They now reach their mark, such as Rui in Phenac City's mayor's house.
Fixed Colosseum and XD reporting a full bag when taking or swapping a Gen 4 held item. Items such as Toxic Orb now return to the bag normally.
Fixed pressing START while waiting for an online challenger crashing Colosseum.
Fixed XD cutscene cameras snapping back and spinning around at higher frame rates. That includes Zook sending out his Shadow Zangoose in Gateon Port.

launcher: New languages: Pokémon XD in French, German, Spanish, Italian and Japanese, and Colosseum in Japanese. Choose the language at the top of Settings → Gameplay; it downloads the first time you play. Colosseum's Japanese pack has Rui in her original outfit.

Update ready: one button in the top bar updates the launcher, then the game, by itself. Each step shows as it goes. With Update automatically off, Play asks whether to update first, and Later waits until the launcher opens again.

Online: players on different game versions can battle, as long as their games battle the same way. A room you can't join says who needs to update, and Update to join gets your update. Everyone needs this launcher to battle online.
Online: rooms take Colosseum and XD players by default. Untick Colosseum and XD players can join for a room for your own game only.

changes: Walk through Rui: in Colosseum, Wes walks straight through Rui instead of pushing her back a step at a time. Turn it off under Gameplay.
Pokémon XD under Generation 4 rules runs end-of-turn effects like Leftovers in speed order, as Platinum does.
Fixed Colosseum vs XD online battles stopping out of sync when two Pokémon had the same speed.
Fixed fast-forward barely speeding up on slower PCs. It only holds back to normal steps while you walk.
Fixed Pokémon XD freezing on the Strategy Memo's Matchup page with a Generation 4 ability.
Fixed a move that hits both foes hitting its user's partner when both foes had fainted, in double battles under Generation 4 rules.
Fixed a side left with no Pokémon out while its trainer still had one to send, in double battles under Generation 4 rules.

launcher: Play Pokémon XD from your own North American disc. Pick Colosseum or XD on the Play page; each game has its own setup folder, disc and memory card, and your Colosseum setup stays as it was.

XD has what Colosseum has: 60 fps, widescreen, HD textures and HD text, Generation 4 and pack Pokémon, the randomizer, Quick moves, shiny Shadow Pokémon, Discord, Add to Steam, save import and export, and the Game Boy Advance link. They use the same settings.
Online: play XD online too, with a party from the team builder or your Story party. Tick Colosseum and XD players can join when you create a room, and players of either game can battle each other.
Watch online battles: a battle under way has a Watch button on the room list.
Online replays: every online battle you play or watch is saved. Watch it again from the new Replays tab on the Online page.
Orre Launcher: the launcher has a new name, for Colosseum and XD. Your settings, games and saves stay where they were.
Choose your hero: play as Wes, Brendan, May, Red or Leaf, or Michael in XD. A New Game asks who you'll be; turn the question off under Gameplay.
Customize: a new tab to colour each hero's outfit on their 3D model and watch them move. Your hero and colours show in the story and online.
Jukebox: a new tab plays the game's music from your disc, and keeps playing while you use the rest of the launcher.
Pokédex: each Pokémon shows its whole evolution family and what each evolution needs. XD's Pokédex shows XD's own models and where to find each Pokémon.
Sound: Master volume, Music and Sound effects sliders under Settings → Sound.

Randomizer: No repeats keeps an evolution family from coming up twice, and First forms starts every starter and Shadow Pokémon at its first stage. Similar strength now spreads its picks instead of repeating the same few Pokémon.
The launcher opens full screen or maximized if that's how you left it.
Windows: setup now works in a folder with an accented letter, such as Pokémon Colosseum, and tries again when Windows can't start a build program (error 0xC0000142).
On Linux, when the game can't open its window, the error now says why.
Fixed Steam's on-screen keyboard popping up on a Steam Deck. It now waits until you press A on a text box.
Fixed the Settings page scrolling to the top by itself while a GameCube controller adapter was plugged in.
Fixed online rooms on Platinum's rules starting their battles without Platinum's rules.
Fixed game updates stopping with "EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory" when the game is on an exFAT or FAT32 drive, such as an SD card or USB drive.

changes: Settings in the game: START's field menu has SETTINGS, with display, graphics and sound options, in Colosseum and XD. Changes are saved to the launcher.
Cheats and warps: F9 opens a cheat menu and F8 takes you anywhere in the game, in Colosseum and XD. Save before warping ahead of the story.
TMs by move: the bag and shops list a TM by the move it teaches, with its number in a tab. Turn it off under Gameplay.
Generation 4 Pokémon blink, close their eyes asleep and change expression during moves, as in Battle Revolution. Press Make assets when the launcher asks.

Later generations: Cherrim changes form in sunlight, Lava Plume and Discharge hit every Pokémon around the user, and under Platinum's rules a fainted Pokémon's replacement comes out at the end of the turn.
Shader warm-up: the game prepares its effects before it needs them, so new places and battles stutter less.
Online: team preview has a cursor, battles use the story's menus, and a battle ends if the two games ever drift apart instead of playing on.
Battle Mode in widescreen: the Pokémon selection and VS screens fill the window instead of showing black bars.
The backtick (`) overlay is now a button guide that lists your own keys and controller buttons.
Fixed the game crashing or freezing when you switched out against Shadow Tag, Arena Trap or Magnet Pull under Platinum's rules.
Fixed Generation 4 move descriptions running out of their boxes.
Fixed a Substitute looking like Turtwig, and Castform's forms turning into Grotle, Torterra or Chimchar.
Fixed U-turn naming the wrong trainer, and Shedinja taking no recoil from Struggle under Platinum's rules.
Fixed cutscenes stopping for good at 60 fps with someone walking on the spot, such as Beluh on the stairs in Agate Village.
Fixed a crash when a trainer walked over to you while Rui stood in the way, such as at the Under's elevator in Pyrite Town.
Fixed the game refusing to save after its save file was left empty, such as by a sudden shutdown.
Fixed walking through walls with fast-forward on, such as beside the Pokémon Center in Agate Village.
Fixed Tab on the keyboard and LB + RB on a controller doing nothing for fast-forward unless you had changed a control. They now work by default, as the Controls page shows.
Fixed fast-forward and faster battle animations waiting for each move's sound to finish.
Fixed sound effects crackling with headphones set to 44.1 kHz on Windows, and with Bluetooth headsets.
Fixed a black party picture and a stuck summary at the Outskirt Stand early in a New Game.
Fixed setting up the game on Windows stopping at a CHANGES file or with a splitlines error.
Language packs: fixed the title's PRESS START looking stretched with a thick outline.

launcher: Later generations: play by Pokémon Platinum's battle rules and add the 107 Generation 4 Pokémon. Turn each on under Settings → Gameplay.
Battle Revolution assets: Generation 4 Pokémon take their looks and cries from your own Battle Revolution disc. Without it, a Colosseum Pokémon stands in for each.
Team builder: give each Pokémon its own moves, held item, ability, nature, EVs and IVs. Bring teams in or out as Pokémon Showdown text. Open it with New party or Edit on the Online tab.
Online formats: Orre Colosseum, Hoenn Stadium and Gen 3 OU rooms, with their clauses and bans. Casual stays as it was, Customise changes any rule, and a room can be a best of 3 or 5.
Online timers: a room can have a turn timer and a battle timer, set when you create it.
Legal Pokémon: format rooms check each Pokémon's moves, held item, EVs and IVs, and say what's wrong. A host can turn the check off under Customise.

Generation 4 online: any room can play by Platinum's rules, and a Generation 4 party battles there with that generation's Pokémon, moves and held items. Choose the rules when you create a room, and Generation 4 at the top of the team builder.
Online battles: both players need this version of the launcher.
Pokémon packs: add Pokémon of your own making, with their own stats, moves, model, sprites and cry. Open the packs folder from the Pokédex, then pick one as a starter or let the randomizer choose it.
Pokédex: models look as they do in the game and blink, every Pokémon has a Shiny look, and Cry plays its cry. It also shows what a Pokémon evolves from.
Randomizer: a run can include Generation 4 Pokémon and the Pokémon of your packs. Tick Gen 4 and Pokémon packs under Randomizer.
Language: play in French, German, Spanish or Italian, or with a fan translation. Choose it under Settings → Gameplay.

Game Boy Advance: link a Generation 3 save to trade Pokémon, register a team and spend Poké Coupons. It works with Ruby, Sapphire, Emerald, FireRed and LeafGreen saves, chosen under Settings → Game Boy Advance, with no GBA BIOS or Game Pak.
Fast-forward: one press of L + R can keep it on, and it runs from 2× to 8×. Set both under Settings → Gameplay.

HD textures: an updated pack keeps the grain of ground and walls and the soft edges of move effects. It also fixes black lines in floors and dark edges on some textures. About 1.9 GB, it downloads the next time you play with HD textures on.
Windows: the game's program has its own icon. The launcher also says before building when the Setup files folder's path has an &, which the build can't use.
When the game stops itself after an error, the launcher says why.
Fixed the game drawing with OpenGL instead of Vulkan on a Steam Deck and other Linux PCs with a newer Mesa.

changes: Generation 4 battle rules: battles play as in Pokémon Platinum, with moves physical or special by themselves, its damage, abilities, held items such as Life Orb and Choice Scarf, and Generation 4's moves. The move list shows whether a move is physical, special or status.

Generation 4 Pokémon: the game's own Pokémon learn moves and evolve as in Platinum, so Yanma, Aipom and Piloswine can become Yanmega, Ambipom and Mamoswine. The Move Deleter at Mt. Battle can also make a Pokémon remember a level-up move.
Choose starters: a New Game asks whether to begin with Espeon and Umbreon. Say No to pick any two Pokémon. Turn the question off under Gameplay in the launcher.
Quick moves: press Z (R1 or RB) in battle to open your moves, then A, B, X or Y to use one. Buttons show as your controller or keyboard has them. It's on to start with; turn it off under Gameplay.
Quick status effects: a status condition or stat change shows where the move hit, without its own camera shot. It's on to start with; turn it off under Gameplay.
The PC has 10 boxes instead of 3, room for 300 Pokémon. Backups keep them all, and a save exported for Dolphin takes boxes 1 to 3.
Shiny Pokémon: a Shadow Pokémon that will be shiny once snagged looks shiny in battle, and Espeon and Umbreon can be shiny from a New Game. Both have switches under Gameplay.
Online battles: Battle Mode's screens surround a battle. Both trainers show before it, you pick your Pokémon on the game's own selection screen when the room has team preview, and the results follow.
Online rules: battles can be doubles and play by Battle Mode's clauses. They now have critical hits and Soul Dew's boost, as the original game's link battles do.
Randomizer: a Shadow Pokémon or trainer's Pokémon that held the item for its type now holds the one for its new type.
Fixed a number showing instead of the move's name when a Pokémon forgets a move in battle.
Fixed the gold labels on the save and Continue screens showing red.
Fixed the sandstorm, strong sunlight, the PDA and the name screen not filling widescreen.
Fixed a stretched box around Sweet Scent's and Confusion's ripple in widescreen.
Fixed the PDA's Snag List showing the original game's Shadow Pokémon in a randomized run.
Fixed the arrow keys and WASD picking nothing on the Pokémon selection screen before a battle.
Fixed PlayStation controllers stopping in the game on Windows a few seconds after it started.
Fixed the game crashing on Mac when a Pokémon's Wish came true.
Fixed a dull echo trailing behind move sounds such as Sing and Attract.
Fixed the game crashing at start-up without a reason when it couldn't read its disc file. It now says what's wrong.
Fixed setup failing with Xcode 26 or pandoc installed, or when Vulkan's downloads fail.

launcher: Online battles: open a room or join one on the new Online tab and battle another player, at level 50 or 100 with 3 or 6 Pokémon each. Build named parties of six from your Pokédex, and your game waits in the stadium until someone joins. The room list updates by itself, and Refresh checks right away.

Story party: battle online with the Pokémon you travel with. The Online tab shows the party in your save, set apart at the top, and brings each one along with its moves, nature, stats, ability, held item and nickname, at the room's level. A party of 3 to 5 can take rooms of 3 each, and Shadow Pokémon stay home until they're purified.
The top bar shows how many players are online. It comes from an anonymous check-in you can turn off under Settings → Launcher.

Show on Discord: while you play, your Discord profile shows where you are in Orre with a picture of the place, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, and online battles show your opponent. The Discord app needs to be open. Turn it off under Settings → Launcher.

Pokédex: browse all 386 Pokémon from your own disc, turn their 3D models around, play their motions and see their shiny looks. It also shows how you can get each one, and locks those the game keeps out of reach. Find it in the new Pokédex tab.

Randomizer: start a New Game with different starters, Shadow Pokémon, trainers' Pokémon and gifts, chosen by a seed you can share. Limit it to the generations you like, keep Pokémon about as strong as those they replace, or leave legendaries out. Your save keeps its seed, so fights stay the same when you try again. Find it under Gameplay.
Export a save: carry on in Dolphin with a .gci file of your game. Find it in the Saves tab.
Battle animations: a speed slider from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1, with 1.5× as the new default, and a Skip battle animations switch that greys it out. Find them under Gameplay.

Macs with Apple Silicon: the game now builds as a native program and draws with Metal, so it runs faster and Rosetta is no longer needed. Metal is the new default renderer on these Macs; Vulkan and OpenGL are still under Graphics. Intel Macs stay on Vulkan.
Fixed the portable launcher on Windows never finding the game's crash reports, so Settings → Launcher can now copy them for a bug report.
Fixed game updates started from Steam filling the activity log with Steam overlay errors, which could also hide why a build failed.
Fixed a crash report on Linux and the Steam Deck when you closed the game with Stop in Steam.

changes: Online battles: two players' games play one battle, with both choosing their moves at the same time, from the launcher's Online tab. A Story party's Pokémon keep their moves, nature, stats, ability, held item, nickname and Poké Ball, at the battle's level.
Save anywhere: the menu you open with Start has a new SAVE option above EXIT. It saves where you stand, and Continue puts you back on that spot.
Randomizer: a new save can be a randomized run, and the save keeps its seed.
Rui and most trainers now have their detailed models in the field too, with sharper faces and real fingers.
Battle animations can run at any speed from 1× to 5× in steps of 0.1.
Macs with Apple Silicon: the game runs natively, and the wipe into a trainer battle plays in full instead of going black.
The game tells the launcher where you are, who you're battling and your lead Pokémon, for Show on Discord.
When Vulkan can't start on Linux, the game now tries the desktop's other window system before falling back to OpenGL, and the message says why Vulkan couldn't start.
In widescreen, the menu you open with Start now sits at the right edge of the screen, as it does in 4:3.
Fixed Pokémon getting a different nature and gender than a GameCube would give them at the same moment, which also threw off the random rolls after it, such as trainers' teams and damage.
Fixed the game not opening its window on Linux with newer graphics drivers, and that error calling the game Super Mario Sunshine.
Fixed people and objects disappearing near the sides of the screen in widescreen.
Fixed the arrow for picking a target sitting away from the status panels in widescreen.
Fixed the stripes of Yes/No boxes stopping short, and the Poké Ball in a text box's corner drawing outside the box, in widescreen.
Fixed Pokémon blinking twice as often at 60 fps, which also used up the game's random numbers faster than on a GameCube.

launcher: HD models: Wes uses his detailed model in the field. Turn it off under Graphics.
The game now builds from the port's own copy of the decompilation.

changes: Wes now has his detailed battle model while walking around, with a sharper face and real fingers.
Fixed the Pokémon faces missing from the Battle Now team screen.
Fixed opposing trainers misjudging a side's conditions and level-based moves.
Fixed the second trainer on a side being mistaken for the first.
Fixed Pokémon faces staying in memory after being replaced.
Fixed the Pokédex seen and caught flags on Linux and macOS.
Fixed Poké Ball catch rates on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the blue background on the main menus and save screen stopping short of the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the PC menus leaving black bars at the sides in widescreen.
Fixed the game crashing when entering a new area after playing for a long time.
Fixed Rui getting stuck walking on the spot when you first enter the mayor's house in Phenac City, and people stalling the same way in other cutscenes.

launcher: Battle animations: moves, send-outs and HP bars play at 2× speed by default. Change to normal speed or 4×, or skip them, under Gameplay.
Add to Steam: play from your Steam library, Big Picture or Game Mode, with artwork. Find it on the main screen, on Windows and Linux.
Skip Launcher: Steam can start the game straight away, and --play does the same from any shortcut.
Graphics presets: Low, Medium, High, Ultra and Steam Deck set the picture all at once. Find them under Graphics.
Crash reports: copy the newest report for a bug report, under Launcher. They stay on your computer.

changes: Fixed a box appearing around the white ring in some battle moves. Their ripple effect now works too.
Fixed your partner walking behind you facing the wrong way on Linux and macOS.
Fixed battle timers always showing 0 on Linux and macOS.
Fixed the title menu's selection jumping to the next option instead of sliding on Linux and macOS.
Fixed reflective effects not showing on Linux and macOS, along with the title options' animation and the stick in the P★DA.
Fixed items and Poké Balls saying they were meaningless to use in battle, and the bag jumping to another pocket afterwards.
Fixed shop messages showing the wrong price and item, like nearly 2 billion for one Super Potion. Sales always paid the right amount.
Fixed the game crashing when you pressed Down in the P★DA's Strategy Memo list.
Installing and updating the game downloads less: it no longer fetches two extra repositories to build.
Battle animations can run at 2× or 4× speed or be skipped, with menus at normal speed and text up long enough to read.
Building the game is faster: its code now compiles once instead of twice, on Windows too.
Setting up the game is quicker: the fixes its code needs now come ready-made instead of being worked out on your computer.
Game updates that change only part of the build now reuse more of what was already compiled.
The first game build after this update takes longer, as it starts over with what it keeps between builds.
Fixed new builds on Linux and macOS leaving out small corrections to battle and menu code that only a rebuild picked up.
Fixed the battle move menu showing the first move's PP and type whichever move you highlighted.
The logo movies at startup now fill a widescreen display with their background colour instead of black bars.

launcher: Fixed Windows builds with your own MSYS2, set with the COLO_MSYS2_ROOT environment variable, looking for the game's compiler in a folder that MSYS2 doesn't have.
Fixed a game download stopping at Prepare port source when a newer game commit is chosen under Settings, Manage game, Game source.
Windows builds now use a compiler that also runs on Windows 7, which the previous one could not.
The first game build on Windows after this update takes longer, as it starts over with the new compiler.

changes: Fixed builds reporting success when the game's compiler couldn't run: they now stop and say why.
Fixed a rare build that left out part of the battle menus' code.
Fixed Battle Now's party check overwriting nearby memory, which stopped the game on Arch Linux.
Fixed the game failing as it started when built on Arch Linux and other systems not based on Debian.
Fixed the game not fully unloading map code it had finished with.

launcher: New launcher background: a painted copper engine out in the desert.
Game updates and rebuilds are much faster: the launcher keeps what it compiled and reuses it. Free up space under Settings, Manage game clears it.
Import a Dolphin save: drop your North American .gci save on the Saves tab, or the folder it is in, and carry on from there. Your current saves are backed up first.
Join our Discord server: the Discord button at the top of the launcher opens the invite in your browser.

changes: The first build of the game is faster too.
Fixed the game stopping on macOS when you arrive in Phenac City with HD textures at the highest resolution.

launcher: First release: set up and play the Pokémon Colosseum PC port from your own North American disc on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Three-step setup downloads everything it needs and builds the game on your computer. The disc image never leaves it.
HD textures: all 7,498 of the game's textures upscaled 4×, on by default. Turn them off under Settings, Graphics.
Settings for the screen format, frame rate, picture sharpness, controls, rumble and GameCube controller adapters.
Your saves are backed up before and after you play. Restore one from the Saves tab.

changes: Native PC port with movies, music and sound, HD text, widescreen, 60 fps and Vulkan or OpenGL rendering.
